units.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp reads and writes PowerPoint presentations in the .pptx format. It supports adding comment authors, comments, and replies to slides, and it allows setting document properties such as title, author, and custom properties.
It creates new presentations from scratch or opens existing .pptx files, adds and removes slides, and saves the result as a .pptx presentation.
It formats text at the character, paragraph, and text-frame level, and applies solid, gradient, pattern, or picture fills and line styles to shapes.
It sets core, application, and custom document properties, adds per-slide speaker notes, and manages comments with authors, timestamps, positions, and replies.
It embeds images from in-memory byte buffers by adding them to the image collection and attaching them to slides as picture frames.
It supports cross-platform builds on multiple operating systems using CMake.
It runs conformance tests defined in the tests directory through continuous integration workflows.
This example creates a new presentation, sets its title, author, and a custom property, and saves it as a PPTX file.
This example adds a comment author, creates a comment and a reply on the first slide, links the reply to the comment, and saves the result as a PPTX file.

The primary entry point is the Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp class, which owns a SlideCollection of Slide objects; each Slide exposes its shapes through ShapeCollection and its per-slide notes through NotesSlideManager.

Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp provides classes for creating, reading, and modifying presentations, including Presentation for document management, SlideCollection and Slide for slide operations, ShapeCollection and its derived shapes for content, and supporting types for text, formatting, tables, images, comments, and document properties.
